editionContext.baseText: Ganjoor online transcription of Ferdowsi’s Shahnameh, its table of contents and the sections named here.

editionContext.scope: The work as a whole, as a map of its reigns and its named stories; no story is told here, and no step of a story is given.

entities.label: The Shahnameh
entities.summary: Ferdowsi’s epic of the kings of Iran from the first king to the Arab conquest, begun about 977 and finished on 8 March 1010; the Aga Khan Museum counts about 50,000 couplets, another source 60,000. It draws on the prose Shahnameh made for Abu Mansur and takes up about a thousand couplets of Daqiqi.

entities.label: Ferdowsi
entities.summary: Abu’l-Qasem Ferdowsi, born in 940 in the village of Baz near Tus in Khorasan, who began the Shahnameh after the death of Daqiqi, finished it in 1010 and died in Tus in 1020 or, more probably, 1025.

facts.text: The poet of the Shahnameh.

entities.label: Daqiqi
entities.summary: The poet who first began to put the Shahnameh into verse; Ferdowsi continued his work after his death, and about a thousand of his couplets stand in the poem.

facts.text: About a thousand couplets of the Shahnameh.

entities.label: Abu Mansur Mohammad ibn Abd al-Razzaq
entities.summary: The lord of Tus for whom the prose Shahnameh, Ferdowsi’s chief source, was compiled in 957.

facts.text: Ordered the prose Shahnameh.

entities.label: The prose Shahnameh of Abu Mansur
entities.summary: A prose book of the kings compiled for Abu Mansur in 957, which became Ferdowsi’s chief source; only its introduction survives.

entities.label: Mahmud of Ghazni
entities.summary: The sultan to whom Ferdowsi dedicated the Shahnameh; he came to the throne in 997.

facts.text: The Shahnameh was dedicated to him.

entities.label: The Pishdadians
entities.summary: The first line of kings in the poem, from Kayumars to Garshasp; scholars call them the Pishdadids. Ganjoor does not use the name as a heading.

entities.label: The Kayanians
entities.summary: The kings of the poem from Kay Qobad, their ancestor, to Dara; Ganjoor does not use the name as a heading.

entities.label: The Ashkanians
entities.summary: The kings after Eskandar, whom the poem treats together in one section as the petty kings.

entities.label: The Sasanians
entities.summary: The kings of the poem from Ardashir to the last Yazdegerd, the house of Sasan.

entities.label: King of Iran, in the poem
entities.summary: The kingship the Shahnameh follows from Kayumars to Yazdegerd, reign by reign.

entities.label: The Florence manuscript
entities.summary: The oldest known manuscript of the Shahnameh, dated 614 AH (1217 CE) and kept in the National Central Library of Florence; it was found there in 1977 and has been published in facsimile.

entities.label: The Baysonghori Shahnameh
entities.summary: A complete illustrated manuscript of 346 folios made in Herat in 1430 for Baysonghor, written in nasta’liq by Ja’far Baysonghori; kept in the Golestan Palace in Tehran.

entities.label: The Shah Tahmasp Shahnameh
entities.summary: The illustrated manuscript made in Tabriz for the Safavid court, begun about 1522 or 1524 and finished about 1537, with 258 paintings; Shah Tahmasp gave it to the Ottoman sultan Selim II in 1568, it was split up after 1970, and its folios are now in several collections, among them the Aga Khan Museum and the Metropolitan Museum.

entities.label: Djalal Khaleghi-Motlagh
entities.summary: The editor of the critical edition of the Shahnameh based on its earliest manuscripts, among them the Florence manuscript; born in Tehran on 11 September 1937.

facts.text: The critical edition of the Shahnameh.

entities.label: The Moscow edition
entities.summary: The edition of the Shahnameh in nine volumes published in Moscow by the Publishing House of Oriental Literature, the first volume in 1960, under the chief editorship of E. E. Bertels.

entities.label: The edition of Khaleghi-Motlagh
entities.summary: The critical edition of the Shahnameh by Djalal Khaleghi-Motlagh in eight volumes; one publisher dates it 1988–2008, another 1987–2005.
